sources.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Mixture of Experts
sources.finding: Already relates routing sensitivity to differences between highly weighted expert functions; theoretical treatment emphasizes smooth MoE, with ImageNet adversarial experiments.
sources.overlap: Function-sensitive routing stability is an established motivation. Our specific sparse top4 numerical boundary and quantum-readout mechanisms need their own empirical contribution.

sources.title: ProbMoE: Differentiable Probabilistic Routing for Mixture-of-Experts
sources.authors: Heng Zhao, Zilei Shao, Guy Van den Broeck, Zhe Zeng
sources.finding: Models cardinality-constrained expert subsets and propagates gradients through exact selection marginals using a surrogate estimator.
sources.overlap: Selection geometry and backward treatment of discrete subsets are studied beyond quantum architectures. Our dense offline counterfactual estimator is a distinct protocol, with its cost recorded.

sources.title: Evidence for Shared Routing Geometry and Dynamics in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
sources.authors: Kirill Labzin, Stepan Kulibaba, Artem Dzhalilov, Artem Gorokhov
sources.finding: Separates generic representation predictability from preserving expert decisions through matched-rank controls and causal transport.
sources.overlap: High feature R2 alone is insufficient for a routing claim; decisions and downstream NLL must be measured separately in our geometry experiments.

sources.title: Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off-Policy Degradation in Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning
sources.finding: Uses rollout/training disagreement to reject stale responses; identifies gradient support bias from replayed routes.
sources.overlap: Off-policy RL drift is separate from our frozen CPU input-roundtrip probe. Do not present current numerical mechanism as an RL mismatch fix.

limits: All report paraphrases must stay compact and distinguish abstract-only reading from full-method verification.
